Title: August 13 2026 City of Boulder City Council Special Meeting and Study Session
Overview: The August 13, 2026 Boulder City Council special meeting and study session opened with a unanimous vote to enter executive session for confidential legal advice on potential new litigation, followed by the study session. Council discussed the process and concerns for the 2027-2030 citywide strategic plan, the Civic Area East bookend development RFP, and the 2026 state and county ballot measures. On ballot measures, council used straw polls to direct staff to draft resolutions opposing the fentanyl and immigration reporting measures and supporting the county child care measure, the graduated income tax, and the education funding measure.

Topic1.Title: Special Meeting: Executive Session Motion and Recess
Topic1.Summary: Council convened the special meeting and held a roll call. Council voted unanimously to call an executive session under state statute and charter section 21A2 to receive confidential legal advice regarding potential new litigation. The motion was properly noticed, and the council recessed into executive session.

Topic2.Title: Executive Session Conclusion and Special Meeting Adjournment
Topic2.Summary: The executive session concluded at about 6 PM with participants identified for the record, and no violations of open meetings law were raised. The special meeting was reconvened and closed at 6:01 PM. The study session then began under Council Member Spear.

Topic3.Title: Strategic Planning Check-In for 2027-2030 Citywide Strategic Plan
Topic3.Summary: Staff presented the process for developing the 2027 through 2030 citywide strategic plan, including a staff advisory team, a world of possibilities document with about 41 inputs drawn from over 170 proposals, and a prioritization tool. Council raised concerns about budget transparency, council ownership of the plan, the scoring methodology, and the need to add items such as Title 9 reform and budget process reform. Staff committed to community engagement in November, a November 14 workshop, and a final draft by January.

Topic4.Title: Civic Area East Bookend Development Partnership RFP
Topic4.Summary: Staff presented the civic area east bookend redevelopment, with an optional west bookend, seeking a private development partner to realize community goals for a year-round farmers market, arts and culture, and food uses connected to Boulder Creek Park. The RFP is planned for late summer 2026, with partner selection in early 2027 and concept planning through 2027. Council asked about selection committee membership, park safety and maintenance costs, phasing, the Arapahoe Pathway, and whether any funding has been secured. Council provided feedback that the goals should be stated more explicitly and that affordability and economic synergy should be considered.

Topic5.Title: 2026 State and County Ballot Measures
Topic5.Summary: Staff summarized the Boulder County early childhood care and education mill levy and several state ballot initiatives, including measures on fentanyl penalties, immigration reporting, transportation funding, the graduated income tax, natural gas rights, and conservation sales tax revenue. Council used straw polls to direct staff to draft resolutions opposing the fentanyl and immigration reporting measures and supporting the county child care measure, the graduated income tax, and the education funding measure. Council did not reach consensus on the conservation sales tax measure, and the transportation and natural gas measures were also opposed.
